title: The Iran War’s Impact on Oil Is Hitting Key Senate Races Hard
gist: Nine months into the Iran war, high diesel, heating oil, and fertilizer prices are shaping key Senate races in Texas, Maine, Ohio and Iowa; the Center for American Progress estimates a cost of at least $1,200 per US household.

insights.claim: Damage to Middle East refineries and uncertainty over the Strait of Hormuz have kept oil prices inflated, costing each US household at least $1,200 per the Center for American Progress.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Oil risk premium is tied to Hormuz status; political pressure may push SPR and tax-relief actions.

insights.claim: Texas diesel prices are up more than 80 percent year over year, about 10 percent above the national average, and Governor Abbott declared a state of emergency.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Diesel tightness hits freight and farm costs; watch for state and federal gas-tax suspensions.
insights.locator: The state, which traditionally had some of the lowest diesel prices

insights.claim: Heating oil prices are nearly double last year's and the Northeast, with over 80 percent of the 4.9 million oil-heated US households, could spend an extra $3.8 billion this winter; the White House released heating oil reserves.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Winter heating demand plus reserve releases create near-term volatility in distillates.
insights.locator: In a sign that the race is uncomfortably close

insights.claim: Middle Eastern nitrogen fertilizer production remains well below prewar levels, and sulfur prices have more than doubled since the start of the year.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Fertilizer input costs pressure farm margins into next planting season.
insights.locator: Nitrogen-based fertilizers, like ammonia and urea

insights.claim: StoneX's Josh Linville says farmers are asking how to lose the least money next year rather than whether they can make money.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Signals reduced planted-area and input-demand risk for ag.
insights.quote: how do I lose the least amount of money next year

insights.claim: Democrats are targeting the war's cost in races including Texas (Talarico vs Paxton, Hinojosa vs Abbott), Maine (Collins vs Jackson), Ohio (Brown vs Husted) and Iowa (Hinson).
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Energy-price politics may drive Senate outcomes and thus energy and tariff policy.
insights.locator: Democrats are trying to use that to their advantage

insights.claim: Some high-ranking Republicans, including Trump, support suspending the federal gas tax.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Gas-tax holiday is a plausible policy response before or after the election.
insights.locator: a move that is supported by some high-ranking Republicans
